transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time, but... well, I guess what finally brought me in is that I just don't feel quite like myself anymore. 

I mean, I'm sure everyone gets into a bit of a rut sometimes, right? But I used to always make time for things—painting, hiking, singing in my choir, and our Sunday family gatherings. I've always been pretty active with all of that. But lately, even when I have a free hour to myself, I just... I just kind of sit there. I can't seem to muster up the energy to care about any of it right now. 

I feel a little silly even complaining about it, but... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things properly.
Have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Well... um, I really don't want to sound overly dramatic, because I know I have so much to be thankful for. But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling that way for a while now. 

It's hard to explain without sounding ungrateful, but most days it just feels like there's this... this heavy gray film over everything. I try my best to push through it and put on a brave face, I really do. But I can be standing right there in the classroom full of students, or just sitting at home with my husband, and I still feel completely hollow inside. And I'll just feel so close to tears, for no good reason at all. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's not a terrible thing to admit. I know I should be handling things better. Does... does that sound like what you're asking about? Am I explaining it okay?
Have you lost interest or felt less pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like painting, hiking, singing, or spending time with your family?

Yes, exactly. Um, like I was trying to say when I first sat down—and I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information—but yes. That's really what finally brought me in, just not feeling like myself at all anymore. 

I used to always make time for my painting, and going hiking, and choir... and I love my family so much, I really do. I know how lucky I am to have them. But lately, even with our Sunday gatherings, or when I just have a free hour to myself, I just... sit there. I can't seem to care about any of it, no matter how hard I try to force myself to be engaged. 

It makes me feel awful to admit that out loud, because I know I should be doing these things and enjoying them like I used to. I feel terribly guilty about it. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question properly.
Have these feelings been affecting your ability to function at work, at home, or in other important areas of your life?

Well... um, I really hate to admit this, because I pride myself on being reliable. I always try to be a good employee and a good wife. But... yes, I suppose it has been affecting things a bit. 

At work—I'm a teaching assistant—I've, um... I've actually missed several teaching sessions recently. And I've sort of been finding ways to avoid the student workshops. I just... I can't seem to keep up with the responsibilities the way I used to, and I'd hate for the students to suffer because I'm not on top of things. 

And at home... well, my husband is just wonderful, he really is. But he's had to step in a lot more lately, because I just kind of... withdraw from our family plans. I just don't feel safe pushing through it all alone right now. 

I feel terribly guilty putting extra work on him and my colleagues. I know I need to be doing better and pulling my weight. Does... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
How long have you been feeling this way? Can you pinpoint when these feelings started or if they’ve happened before?

Well... um, I really hope this doesn't make me sound like I can't handle my responsibilities, because I usually do try so hard to keep everything running smoothly. But... I suppose it's been building up for a while now. 

I'd say... maybe about eight months? It sort of started right around the time I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative at work. Which is a wonderful opportunity, it really is, and I'm so grateful they trusted me with it. I just... I think maybe I haven't been managing the extra pressure as well as I should be. I've never really felt quite like this before, not for this long anyway. 

I hope it's okay that it's been going on that long before I came in. I just kept thinking I could fix it myself if I just worked a little harder. Does that... does that answer your question? Is eight months the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Have you ever felt this way before, with similar feelings of sadness or loss of interest, or is this the first time you’ve experienced something like this?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt a little stressed or overwhelmed, you know, just normal things that everyone goes through when they're trying to balance work and family. But I always managed to bounce back pretty quickly. 

So, no, I've never felt... quite like this. Not where it just lingers and makes it so hard to do the things I know I'm supposed to be doing. I've always prided myself on being pretty resilient, so it's a bit embarrassing to admit that this is the first time I just... can't seem to shake it off. 

I hope that's okay, that this is the first time. I know some people deal with this their whole lives, and I feel a little silly complaining about it when it's only been these past eight months. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of it than I should be.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually high, overly energetic, or irritable for several days or more, where it was out of character for you?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I mean, I try very hard to keep an even temper, you know? Sometimes I might get a tiny bit irritable if I'm just exhausted from grading papers or running the workshops, but... I always try my best to keep it to myself so I don't bother my husband or my coworkers with it. I really hate the idea of taking my stress out on other people.

I hope that's okay. I know you're asking for a reason, and I hope I'm not giving you the wrong answer or leaving anything important out. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful. Is... is that what you needed to know?
